title: Don't mind the gap: Absolutely Continuous Edge Spectrum in a Mobility Gap
abstract: We study the edge spectrum of two-dimensional lattice Hamiltonians and magnetic Schrödinger operators in a mobility gap, an energy interval in which the bulk spectrum is potentially localized rather than necessarily absent. Under suitable localization and boundary assumptions, we prove that a constant nonzero bulk topological index implies that the entire interval belongs to the absolutely continuous spectrum of the corresponding half-space operator. The absolutely continuous spectral multiplicity is bounded below by the absolute value of the index at almost every energy in the interval. The first version of the auxiliary-space cut construction in Section 2.3 was generated using ChatGPT 6.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a deep link between bulk topology and edge spectrum for lattice Hamiltonians in a mobility gap. By using index theory, the authors prove that a constant, non-zero bulk topological index guarantees a minimum, non-zero absolutely continuous spectral multiplicity on the corresponding half-space operator. This is crucial for understanding robust edge states in disordered or gapped quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a non-zero bulk topological index in a mobility gap forces the existence of an absolutely continuous spectrum in the corresponding half-space Hamiltonian.
main_result: It proves that if the bulk topological index is a non-zero constant over an interval, the absolutely continuous spectral multiplicity of the half-space operator is bounded below by the absolute value of that index for almost every energy in the interval.
method: The proof utilizes advanced index theory (Fredholm index) and unitary scattering theory, constructing an auxiliary-space cut to transfer bulk topological information to the physical half-space spectrum.
model_or_system: The analysis applies to two-dimensional lattice Hamiltonians and magnetic Schrödinger operators, considering both discrete ($\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^2)$) and continuous ($L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$) settings.
key_observables: Absolutely continuous spectral multiplicity ($	ext{mac}(E; bH)$) and the bulk topological index ($C$).
important_parameters: The existence of a 'mobility gap' (an energy interval where the bulk spectrum is potentially localized) and the constancy of the bulk index $C$ over an interval $\Delta$.
main_assumptions: The theorem requires suitable localization and boundary assumptions (e.g., (D1)-(D4) or (C1)-(C4)).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometry, comparing the auxiliary cut to the physical boundary and showing the forced absolutely continuous component in the half-space spectrum.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general index theory (Section 2.2) to establishing a key lemma linking the index to the minimum absolutely continuous multiplicity (Lemma 2.2), culminating in the main theorem (Theorem 1.1) which applies the index machinery to the half-space operator.
why_interesting: The connection between topological invariants (like the index) and the spectral structure (like $\sigma_{ac}$) is fundamental in modern condensed matter theory, particularly for understanding edge states in topological insulators.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Geometry and spectral conclusion of Theorem 1.1. (a) The solid horizontal line is the boundary of the upper half-space and the dashed vertical line is the auxiliary cut used in the index construction. Dots and rings indicate localization centers and localized full-space eigenfunctions. (b) The same interval ∆is shown for the full-space operator H and the half-space operator bH. Localized full-space spectrum may occur in ∆, whereas a nonzero index C forces an absolutely continuous component of bH with mac(E; bH) ≥|C| for almost every E ∈∆. The ticks are schematic and do not represent isolated eigenvalues; additional singular spectrum is not excluded.
